I read the whole file and searched the repository and Mathlib for related uses. The file has no @[simp] attributes or custom simp sets. Its simp calls are `simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hx ⊢`, `simp only [f, QuotientAddGroup.lift_mk] at this` and `simpa [g] using this`. All three are local, and I saw no sign of competing rules, unwanted expansion or a rewrite cycle.

The one candidate was `mem_orthogonal` (line 171), which is proved by `Iff.rfl` and has no @[simp] attribute. Mathlib marks the analogous `mem_orthogonalBilin_iff` and the bilinear-form `mem_orthogonal_iff` as @[simp]. I did not report it, because nothing in the file or the repository uses `mem_orthogonal` in a simp call. The proofs that touch `orthogonal` use definitional unfolding or `rw`, so I found no downstream use that an attribute would improve. The remaining declarations (`nsmul_natCard_eq_zero`, the torsion bounds and the card inequalities) are non-simp statements with hypotheses, where simp annotations would not be appropriate. I did not run Lean, so this is a judgment from reading the sources.
